next_question: Does any published system or benchmark report a CROSS-SITE TRANSFER result - mechanisms learned on one set of real websites and then executed on a held-out set of never-seen websites - as four separately measurable quantities on a stated denominator (transfer success on a stated N of held-out sites, execution correctness conditional on resolution, abstention-or-refusal rate, and either a stated boilerplate-exclusion rule or an explicit split of task/actionable structure from shared HTML template boilerplate), together with its holdout rule (leave-one-site-out or equivalent, no site-identity leakage) and its denominators; and specifically, does any such report isolate the site-pair-specific stratum from the ubiquitous-template stratum? FALSIFIER: no source publishes a cross-site transfer rate in that four-part form with a stated holdout split, in which case C-CROSSSITE has NO external numeric comparator, the registry next_gate 'true website holdout without site identity leakage' must be set internally, and the external-bar question is closed in the negative FOR THAT CORPUS ONLY, with bounded recall over the mandate's target list recorded exactly. A negative is worth having only if the search can actually fail, so the design must carry the fixes this cycle and its predecessor exposed rather than repeating a self-fulfilling null: (i) resolve every target name to a verified artifact identity BEFORE scoring any condition, and record 'not located' as UNMEASURED and never as a system-level negative - that single omission is exactly how the predecessor's mandated target COVENANT, 1 of 5, was silently substituted by arXiv:2608.02680 and lost; (ii) include a null control with power against the failure that actually occurred, i.e. inject a deliberately wrong artifact identity or a deliberately shared-boilerplate corpus and require the pipeline to flag it, since the predecessor's NC-FABRICATED-BINDING-CLAIMS searched for three literal phrases no paper would contain and detected nothing while a target identity was being substituted underneath it; (iii) require every reported number to carry its accounting convention, its denominator and its holdout rule, so that a corpus figure cannot be mistaken for a rate. CONTINGENCY IF NEGATIVE, recorded here as routing rather than as a second question: C-CROSSSITE's internal bar must then be set by a statistic that is NOT invariant to host relabelling paired with a null built on a permutation that IS - the frozen AGF here is provably invariant under eTLD+1 relabelling, 1 distinct value over 1,000 permutations bitwise equal to the point estimate - and that statistic must partition shared HTML template boilerplate from site-pair-specific task structure, because on this packet's 155 pages 97.25% of matched instances were list signatures and only 3.51% came from the site-pair-specific 2-5-host regime a cross-site inheritance product would monetise. That internal work belongs to C-CROSSSITE's owner lanes (physics, graph, frontier), not to Intel.
why_next: This packet is the first credential-free, fully completed real-Web measurement in the C-CROSSSITE thread, and it split cleanly along the two halves the mandate asked for, which is what makes the next question knowable rather than guessable. One half is now measured and needs no further work: the per-observation cost floor for a minimal HTTP+HTML structural representation is 763.06 tokens / 2,801.19 bytes (median 576 / 2,138) over n=155 observations from 15 eTLD+1 hosts, 22.0x to 68.2x smaller in tokens than the three preregistered baselines measured on the same observations, with every paired bootstrap CI upper bound strictly negative. The other half is not measured and cannot be measured by this design, for a reason that is now proven rather than suspected: the frozen estimator and the frozen null are the same function of the data up to a relabelling, so the primary clause is x>x and 1,000 permutations of the host labels produced exactly one distinct value, bitwise equal to the observed point estimate. What that failure bought is a completed, reproducible, credential-free substrate and a decomposition that says something specific rather than nothing: only 67 distinct signature keys are shared across the 15 hosts, they carry all 416,218 matched instances, 97.25% of those are list signatures, a single key (list(ul, /{slug}/{slug})) is 49.56% of them, 96.49% come from keys carried by 6 or more of the 15 hosts, and only 3.51% come from the site-pair-specific 2-5-host regime that a cross-site inheritance product would actually monetise. So the addressable stratum is now known to be small on this sample, and it is not known whether it is above its own null. Two consequences follow, and they point at different lanes. First, the internal question - is the 3.51% site-pair-specific stratum real, or is it the residue of a shared HTML template vocabulary? - belongs to C-CROSSSITE's owner lanes (physics, graph, frontier) and is the only route to a bar, because the audit records that this packet produced no external baseline for prevalence and the registry next_gate 'true website holdout without site identity leakage' is therefore still unset. Second, the external question proposed in next_question is Intel's own charter work and is the missing half of the mandate, which explicitly asked that SPIDER's external baseline set be set by measurement rather than by reported numbers: on the observation-cost side that request is now answered, and on the cross-site-transfer side it is untouched. Why that question rather than a repeat of this packet's shape: the thread has now burned one packet on a prevalence measurement that returned x>x, and the parent's lesson generalises exactly - a search that cannot fail produces a self-fulfilling null, whether it is a literature sweep that looked for three literal phrases or a permutation null that is an algebraic identity. Both of the design repairs needed for the next search (identity-before-scoring, a control with power against the failure that actually occurred) are already named in this cycle's audit and in the predecessor's, and they are cheap. Why the boilerplate split is demanded in the external question rather than treated as an internal nicety: the specific trap this packet fell into is that an aggregate structural-similarity endpoint is blind to the failure mode, because ubiquitous HTML boilerplate and genuine site-pair-specific task structure both raise it. Any external cross-site number that does not state its boilerplate-exclusion rule or its holdout rule cannot distinguish the same two things, so demanding that rule in the external corpus is the same discrimination the internal statistic needs. Beneficiaries: physics/graph/frontier get an explicit, cheap, already-implemented route to a powered statistic and a named stratum to test; product gets a conventioned cost floor with denominators for the shared per-span cost ledger and, equally important, a documented reason not to build the product thesis on cross-site inheritance until the 3.51% stratum is shown to be real; the Global Research Director gets a decision input that was previously blocked - four prior packets on the HF_TOKEN-gated WebGym census route produced nothing usable, and this route completed with zero credentials.

established: THE PER-OBSERVATION COST FLOOR, and it is the only frozen decision-relevant finding in this packet that is both valid and evaluable. A minimal HTTP+HTML structural representation costs 763.058064516129 tokens and 2801.1870967741934 bytes per observation on average (median 576 tokens / 2138 bytes), over n=155 observations from 15 of the 20 pre-registered eTLD+1 hosts. All three preregistered baselines were computed on the SAME 155 observations under the SAME tokenizer (cl100k_base, n_vocab 100277), so the ratios are tokenizer-robust: B-RAW-HTML 52020.348387096776 tokens / 151741.4129032258 bytes (68.17x tokens), B-FULL-DOM 50907.33548387097 / 145140.81935483872 (66.71x tokens, 51.81x bytes), B-A11Y-TREE preregistered approximation 16793.670967741935 / 48693.051612903226 (22.01x tokens, 17.38x bytes). Paired eTLD+1-level bootstrap, 10,000 replicates: 95% CI upper bound for (tokens_minimal - tokens_full_dom) is -22823.814833333337 and for (tokens_minimal - tokens_a11y) is -8932.249000000002, both strictly negative; mean differences -50144.27741935484 and -16030.612903225807. Minimal is smaller than full DOM on 155/155 observations, than the a11y approximation on 150/155 (96.77%), and than raw HTML on 155/155. The frozen prereg section 12 cost clause is SATISFIED. (audit baseline_findings[0..3]; recomputed_metrics.cost_per_observation_mean, .cost_paired_differences; result.json metrics.cost_per_observation_mean, .cost_paired_differences, .cost_ratios_mean_baseline_over_minimal)

THE FROZEN PRIMARY CLAUSE IS UNEVALUABLE, AND THE REASON IS PROVEN ALGEBRAICALLY, NOT MERELY OBSERVED. AGF = sum_K (T_K^2 - sum_s n_{s,K}^2) / (2 * total_signatures) depends on the per-host key counts n_{s,K} only through the symmetric quantity sum_s n_{s,K}^2. Permuting the eTLD+1 labels is a bijection on hosts, so it permutes (n_{s,K})_s and leaves every sum_s n_{s,K}^2, hence every T_K, hence AGF exactly invariant. Empirically: 1,000 permutations produced exactly 1 distinct AGF value, 83.51083467094703, bitwise equal to the observed point estimate, with std = 0.0, min = p50 = p95 = p99 = max all identical; the frozen secondary metric mean pairwise Jaccard likewise took exactly 1 distinct value. The frozen primary clause therefore reduces to 83.51083467094703 > 83.51083467094703 and carries no information. result.json records primary_evaluable = false and primary_satisfied = null, NOT false. (audit required_fixes[0]; audit validity_findings[0]; result.json controls.NC-SHUFFLED-HOST pass=false with the algebraic pass_reason; report.md section 3)

THE FROZEN 2-HOST POSITIVE-CONTROL THRESHOLD IS ARITHMETICALLY UNREACHABLE. prereg 11.2 expected AGF > 0.8 from two synthetic hosts, but under the frozen 7.3 definition a 2-host design caps at exactly 0.5: with n signatures per host, all keys distinct and matched 1:1, matched instances = n and total signatures = 2n, so AGF = n/2n = 0.5 whatever the fixture contains. Observed 0.5833333333333334 exceeds that ceiling only because 2 of the 14 matched instances come from duplicated keys. (audit required_fixes[1]; result.json controls.PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS frozen_numeric_threshold_met=false, frozen_numeric_threshold_reachable=false; report.md section 4)

THE EXTRACTION AND COMPARISON PIPELINE CAN BOTH DETECT KNOWN CORRESPONDENCE AND DISCRIMINATE UNRELATED STRUCTURE, confirmed against nulls that have power. On the frozen 2-host synthetic alias pair, mean pairwise Jaccard = 1.0 (identical signature sets, 12 shared keys, 1 of 1 pairs nonzero) against the NC-SIG-REASSIGN Jaccard p95 of 0.8181818181818182, and AGF 0.5833 against that null's AGF p95 of 0.5. On the non-frozen 4-host extension, the one related pair gives Jaccard 1.0 and 5 of 6 unrelated pairs give exactly 0.0, with observed Jaccard 0.16667 above that null's p95 of 0.1645546814296814. PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS therefore passes on its stated purpose; only its numeric threshold is a design defect. (audit validity_findings[4]; result.json controls.PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS pass=true, PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS-4SITE-POWER-EXTENSION pass=true with its honest underpower note; report.md section 4)

THE ONLY NULL AVAILABLE WITH POWER POINTS BELOW THE OBSERVED SHARING, and it is explicitly non-frozen and decision-not-used. NC-SIG-REASSIGN permutes the pooled signature multiset across hosts while preserving every host's signature count and the global multiset exactly: 869 distinct AGF values over 1,000 permutations (std 0.19345684094637847, p95 102.09313804173355) and jaccard p95 0.37740084088184633. Observed AGF 83.51 is 18.58230337078652 BELOW that p95; observed mean pairwise Jaccard 0.1267 is 0.250679507556543 BELOW it. The direction holds on the typed-slot population (observed 80.04368932038835 vs p95 100.67478762135923, -20.63). The audit validates the construction as a test of 'does host grouping carry structure beyond the shared vocabulary' and states the limit in terms: this does NOT show absence of reusable task structure, because the statistic cannot distinguish boilerplate from task structure, and it is not a bounded negative on C-CROSSSITE. The clause AGF_point > null_p95 AND AGF_CI_lower > null_p95 reduces to 83.51083467094703 > 83.51083467094703, so it can be neither satisfied nor falsified. What is rejected is the test, not the prevalence hypothesis. (audit required_fixes[0]; result.json metrics.decision_rule_evaluation)

REJECTED, bounded to this packet: the frozen 2-host positive control's numeric threshold AGF > 0.8 as a sensitivity criterion, and the frozen validity sub-condition null_std > 0 as a diagnostic. The former is unreachable by construction (a 2-host design caps at 0.5) and the latter can only ever fail, because the null is an algebraic identity rather than a weak sample. REJECTED, bounded to this packet's estimator and this 15-host sample: reading the AGF magnitude 83.51083467094703, or the typed-slot sensitivity value 80.04368932038835, as a prevalence FRACTION or as a number comparable with any externally reported prevalence. The estimator is unbounded above by construction - one signature can match on every host pair - so prereg 7.3's 'fraction' wording is an error; the typed-slot rule templates any single-segment path to /{slug}, letting structurally unlike sites share a template, and 66.13162118780096% of signatures carry at least one typed slot, which inflates the statistic in every population including the nulls. (audit required_fixes[6],[7]; result.json metrics.frozen_primary_metric.unit, .sensitivity_typed_slot_population_not_frozen; result.json validity_notes[12])

REJECTED as a reading, bounded: that the 22.01x accessibility-tree token ratio is the advantage over a real browser accessibility tree. B-A11Y-TREE is the preregistered approximation built from semantic HTML elements, roles, aria-* attributes and heading levels, and no browser binary was available while the frozen prereg forbids requiring one. It is a LOWER bound on true accessibility-tree cost, so the 22.0x is an UPPER bound on the real advantage, and the true advantage is unknown and could be materially smaller. (audit required_fixes[8]; result.json controls.B-A11Y-TREE.residual_limitation, validity_notes[5])

REJECTED, bounded to this 15-host sample and this frozen statistic: the reading that the measured cross-site sharing constitutes evidence FOR an addressable cross-site inheritance market, and equally the design conclusion that 'the Web is built from <ul> elements' is a market finding. Under the only powered null available the observed sharing sits 18.58 AGF units and 0.2507 Jaccard units BELOW a random re-partition of the same vocabulary, 97.25% of the 416218 matched instances are list signatures, a single key is 49.56% of them, and 96.49% come from keys carried by 6+ of the 15 hosts. This rejects the frozen statistic's value as a market indicator. It is explicitly NOT a bounded negative on C-CROSSSITE, because the statistic cannot distinguish reusable task structure from shared HTML boilerplate, and the NC-SIG-REASSIGN randomisation is producer-constructed, non-frozen and reserved by the auditor for independent confirmation. (audit claim_ceiling; audit unresolved[3]; audit recomputed_metrics.powered_null_NC_SIG_REASSIGN_not_frozen.interpretation)
unknown: Whether alias-generalizable cross-site TASK structure, as opposed to shared HTML boilerplate, exists at all in a form SPIDER could inherit. The frozen statistic cannot separate the two, and neither can the powered supplementary null, because both are computed on the same signature vocabulary. This is the central open fact and it is unmeasured, not answered in either direction.

Whether the 3.51% site-pair-specific stratum (keys carried by 2 to 5 of the 15 hosts) is above its OWN null. On this sample it is 3.51% of matched instances, which is the only regime a cross-site inheritance product would monetise, but no powered test of that stratum exists. This is the cheapest single internal falsifier that could bound the market thesis at its root, and it is unmeasured.

The per-observation cost floor for a client-rendered site. NOT_MEASURED. Blocking artefacts: no browser binary in this environment, and zero same-origin anchor hrefs in crates.io's raw HTML (HTTP 200, client-rendered application). Smallest unblocking action: a credential-free rendering substrate, or an explicit product decision to bound the thesis to static-HTML sites. (provenance.json dataset.not_measured; audit unresolved[1])

Whether the 4 User-Agent-blocked hosts (npmjs.com, sourceforge.net, stackoverflow.com) and the 2 zero-anchor hosts (crates.io, kernel.org) would change the prevalence decomposition, and whether the 3 redirect-crossed entries would. The frozen prereg forbids adaptive sampling, so no alternative User-Agent, renderer, base URL or sample was probed. (audit unresolved[2])

Whether the powered-null direction is robust. NC-SIG-REASSIGN is one defensible randomisation among several, constructed by the producer rather than by the frozen design; the auditor validated it as a test of whether host grouping carries information beyond the shared vocabulary but explicitly flagged that its choice must be independently confirmed before any lane re-scopes on its direction. It also does not discriminate AGF at the 4-host control size, where the null lattice is coarse enough to reach the observed 0.4666666666666667 - that is underpower at 30 signatures, not a negative result. (audit unresolved[3]; result.json controls.PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS-4SITE-POWER-EXTENSION.residual_limitation)

Whether a more conservative template extractor reduces the boilerplate share. Requiring >=2 path segments or a semantic role before admitting a typed slot would change both the observed and the null populations, and was never run. 66.13% of signatures currently carry at least one typed slot. (audit unresolved[4])

Whether no external baseline number exists for cross-site prevalence, or whether one exists and this program has not found it. The audit records that this packet produced no usable external bar for prevalence, so C-CROSSSITE's registry next_gate 'true website holdout without site identity leakage' is still unset, and the mandate's request to set SPIDER's external baseline set by measurement rather than by reported numbers is answered only on the observation-cost side, with 3 internal baselines measured on the same 155 observations. (audit unresolved[5])

Whether the 66.7x and 22.0x cost advantages survive a rendering substrate. They are ratios of HTTP-observable representations; a JS-executed DOM or a real browser accessibility tree could close much of the gap, and that was not measured.

Whether the 15-host sample's documentation/reference/foundation skew changes any conclusion. 4 of the 5 failures were edge blocks of the frozen User-Agent, so the surviving sample is biased toward the least e-commerce-like members of the frozen 20; the direction and size of that bias on the prevalence side are unknown.
